Subject: Initial intake - dedicated capacity for Novacorp

Alex — thanks for the quick intro last week. Novacorp is ready to start sizing for a committed dedicated footprint. High-level goals: reduce median latencies for our chat assistant, guarantee capacity for peak shopping events, and move sensitive workloads into a private/dedicated environment.

Quick context:
- Expected monthly calls: ~2,150,000 (text generation + some embeddings)
- Typical prompt length: 80–160 tokens (median ~120)
- Typical response length: 300–800 tokens (median ~520)
- Peak concurrent active sessions (worldwide): ~800 (95th ~1,200 during flash sale spikes)
- Streaming: ~60% of sessions require streaming (progressive token emission)
- Embeddings: ~1.1M vectors / month (512-d float)
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II required; retention: session logs retained 30 days, audit logs 1 year.

Can you send your pre-sales sizing questionnaire and any baseline assumptions you need? We're also evaluating a 90-day POC followed by a committed reserve for 6–12 months. Timeline: hope to finalize footprint and budget before end of Q3.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if that helps.

— Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear context. Attaching our dedicated-capacity intake PDF (short form) — please fill what you can. I pasted the main questions below for convenience.

Key items we need to produce a baseline estimate:
- Per-region RPS and expected percentage of traffic per region (US/EU/APAC)
- Concurrency profile by hour of day and expected flash-sale multipliers
- Distribution of models (e.g., Llama-3-70B for chat, smaller for reranking) and whether you want quantized weights or FP16/AMP
- Expected ratio of streaming vs non-streaming sessions (you noted ~60%)
- Token length distribution (percentiles for prompt/response) and any long-tail workflows (>2k tokens)
- Embedding batch sizes and latency SLOs for embedding endpoints
- Retention & encryption requirements (KMS/HSM) and whether data will be in a VPC/on-prem

Quick assumptions I'm going to use for an initial sizing run (we'll refine after you return the sheet):
- Recommendation baseline uses H100-class instances for the primary chat model; A10G/4090-class for embedding workers and small-model endpoints
- KV/prefix caching expected to cut steady-state token generation by ~15–25% depending on reuse — we'll want a prompt sample to estimate this
- For streaming sessions we assume an additional 10–20% overhead on concurrency due to late-binding connections and smaller batch sizes

Next steps: fill the attached form and I'll run a quick top-line footprint + cost delta and send a recommended baseline (GPU counts, node types, autoscale buffer) + a proposed 90-day POC plan. If it's easier, let's do a 30-min intake call Wednesday.

Cheers,

Alex — attached is our completed intake sheet. Highlights: 
- Region split: US 65%, EU 25%, APAC 10%
- Hourly concurrency: baseline 450–650, daily peak 700–800, promotional spike multiplier x1.8 (~1,200) for 2–3 hours, expected ~3 promo days/month
- Token distributions: prompt P50 120, P90 180, P99 420; response P50 520, P90 780, P99 1,600 (long-tail occasionally to 3k)
- Streaming: 60% streaming; avg stream duration 7–12s; 40% non-streaming generation
- Models: Primary chat Llama-3-70B (prefer quantized if quality is preserved), reranker: Llama-2-13B or smaller, embeddings on a distilled 3B model
- Embedding batches: 64–128, 95th latency target 300ms for batch embeddings
- Latency SLOs: 95th token latency for streaming <800ms end-to-end; non-streaming gen P95 <900ms
- Data residency: US-only for PII flows; SOC2 Type II compliance required; KMS integration preferred

Also included procurement contact (procurement@novacorp.com) and preferred cadence for POC billing. Let me know if you want a sample of the prompt corpus to estimate cache hit rates.

Thanks — Elena

Elena / Rajiv — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sheet — very helpful. Quick baseline recommendation based on the supplied distribution and our internal perf profiles: 

Baseline (sustained target for production):
- Hardware: 10 H100-equivalent GPUs (normalized compute). Suggest 4x 4-GPU nodes (or single-node equivalents) with local NVMe for KV cache.
- Autoscale buffer: reserve capacity to burst to 16 H100-equivalents for promo spikes (this handles x1.8 multiplier at P99 with safety margin).
- Streaming config: separate streaming front-ends sized to handle 60% sessions with smaller batch windows; expect ~15% higher concurrency for streaming handling.
- Embeddings: 3x A10G-equivalent workers with batching (64–128) and a dedicated inference queue to keep embedding P95 <300ms.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache; our estimate from sample prompt sets suggests a 15–20% token reduction (we'd validate with a prompt sample).
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit (nf4) quant for primary Llama-3-70B on H100 if internal QA confirms minimal quality regression; keep FP16 fallback route for rare long-tail flows >2k tokens.
- Networking: colocate regionally (US primary), private VPC peering for lower egress jitter; ensure KMS in-region for keys.

POC plan (90 days):
- Deploy a Dedicated cluster with 6 H100-equivalents for the first 30 days to validate latency, caching benefits, and quantization.
- After validation, scale to the 10 H100 baseline for 60 days while monitoring cost/QoE and tweak autoscale triggers.
- Deliverables: baseline capacity report, observed cache hit rates, perf/regression evals on prompt set, and a finalized reserved capacity contract.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will share a preliminary committed pricing and POC budget.
2) Dev will provide a short tech note on quantization path and KV cache sizing.
3) Procurement: can you confirm preferred invoice terms and PO contact?

If that matches expectations I can draft a short SOW and POC statement of work. Happy to run a walkthrough of the baseline numbers on Monday.

Cheers,
